description: Gross Rent Multiplier — the ratio of property value to gross annual (or monthly) rental income, derived from comparable sales. Applied to the subject property's gross rent to estimate value under the GRM approach. Populated when approach_type = GRM.

description: Projected investment hold period in years used in the DCF analysis. Defines the number of annual cash flow periods modeled before the terminal reversion value is calculated. Typically ranges from 5 to 15 years for commercial real estate. Populated for DCF approach type.

description: Internal Rate of Return — the discount rate at which the net present value of all projected cash flows (including acquisition cost and terminal reversion) equals zero. Key investment performance metric output from the DCF model. Populated for DCF approach type.
reference: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise; CFA Institute — Real Estate Valuation

description: IVSC IVS 105 methodology classification code identifying the specific valuation technique applied (e.g., IVS105-IC for Income Capitalization, IVS105-CA for Cost Approach, IVS105-SC for Sales Comparison). Supports regulatory compliance documentation and cross-border reporting.

description: Estimated market value of the land component as if vacant and available for its highest and best use. Used in the cost approach as the foundation to which depreciated cost of improvements is added. Populated for cost approach type.

description: Free-text field capturing appraiser commentary on the rationale, assumptions, limitations, and adjustments specific to this valuation approach. Supports IVSC IVS 105 compliance, USPAP disclosure requirements, and peer review documentation.

description: Net Operating Income — EGI minus total OPEX. The primary income metric used in direct capitalization and DCF valuation. Represents the annual pre-debt, pre-tax cash flow generated by the property. Populated for direct_cap and DCF approach types.
reference: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

description: Net Present Value — the sum of all discounted future cash flows minus the initial investment cost, as output by the DCF model. A positive NPV indicates value creation above the required return. Populated for DCF approach type.
reference: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise; FASB ASC 820

description: Potential Gross Income — the maximum annual rental revenue the property could generate at 100% occupancy at market rent. Used as the starting point for income capitalization approaches (direct cap and DCF). Populated for direct_cap and DCF approach types.
reference: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

description: Loss in value attributable to physical deterioration of the improvements, including curable deferred maintenance and incurable structural wear. Deducted from RCN in the cost approach. Populated for cost approach type.

description: Basis on which the concluded market rent is expressed. Indicates whether the rent is annual or monthly and the lease structure (NNN — Triple Net, gross, or modified gross) that underpins the income analysis.

description: Replacement Cost New (RCN) — the estimated cost to construct a building of equivalent utility using current materials, standards, and design at current prices. Starting point for the cost approach before depreciation deductions. Populated for cost approach type.

description: Narrative description of key sensitivity scenarios tested for this approach, such as the impact of a 25 bps change in CAP rate or discount rate on concluded value. Supports investment decision-making and risk disclosure in appraisal reports.

description: Risk-adjusted discount rate applied in the DCF model to calculate NPV and present value of projected cash flows. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0750 = 7.50%). Reflects required rate of return for the investment strategy.

description: Ratio of NOI to total debt service (principal and interest) for the period. A DSCR above 1.0 indicates the property generates sufficient income to cover debt obligations. Critical metric for lenders and CMBS compliance.
reference: CMBS Underwriting Standards; FASB; Yardi Voyager — Accounts Payable

description: Actual gross income collected during the period after deducting vacancy and credit loss from PGI. EGI = PGI minus vacancy and credit loss. Core revenue metric for property-level performance.
reference: NCREIF; Appraisal Institute; Argus Enterprise — Cash Flow Modeling

description: Projected CAP rate applied to the terminal year NOI to calculate the asset's residual/terminal value at the end of the hold period. Expressed as a decimal. Key assumption in DCF terminal value calculation.
reference: Appraisal Institute; IVSC; Argus Enterprise — Valuation

description: Projected investment hold period in years as modeled in the DCF analysis. Determines the time horizon over which cash flows are projected and the terminal value is calculated.
reference: Argus Enterprise — Investment Analysis; ULI

description: Internal Rate of Return calculated on the asset's equity cash flows after accounting for debt financing. Expressed as a decimal. Reflects the return to equity investors after leverage effects.
reference: NCREIF; CFA Institute; Argus Enterprise — Investment Analysis

description: Ratio of outstanding debt to current appraised or market value of the asset. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.6500 = 65%). Key leverage metric for lenders, CMBS covenants, and portfolio risk management.
reference: CMBS Underwriting Standards; FASB; Federal Reserve Guidance

business_glossary_term: Net Leasable Area in Square Feet (NLA SQF)
description: Net leasable area of the property in square feet as of the performance period. Used as the denominator for PSF metrics (OPEX PSF, revenue PSF) and occupancy calculations.
reference: BOMA Standards; RESO Data Dictionary

description: Net Operating Income for the period calculated as EGI minus operating expenses. Primary measure of a property's income-generating ability before debt service and capital expenditures. SSOT metric for investment performance.
reference: NCREIF; Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 842; Argus Enterprise

description: Net Present Value of the asset's projected cash flows discounted at the model's discount rate. Positive NPV indicates value creation above the required return threshold. Sourced from Argus Enterprise DCF model.
reference: CFA Institute; Argus Enterprise — Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling

description: Percentage of total leasable area that is occupied and generating income during the performance period. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9150 = 91.50%). Core leasing performance indicator.
reference: RESO Data Dictionary; NCREIF; CoStar Suite — Property Analytics

description: Total property-level operating expenditures for the period including property management fees, insurance, taxes, utilities, repairs, and CAM costs. Excludes debt service and capital expenditures.
reference: NCREIF; FASB ASC 842; Yardi Voyager — General Ledger

business_glossary_term: Operating Expense Per Square Foot (OPEX PSF)
description: Total operating expenses divided by the property's net leasable area in square feet. Expressed as currency per square foot (PSF). Enables cross-property benchmarking of operating efficiency.
reference: BOMA Standards; NCREIF; CoStar Suite — Property Analytics

description: Last day of the reporting period for which this asset performance record is calculated. Together with performance_period_start_date defines the measurement window.

description: Granularity of the performance measurement period. Determines whether the record represents a monthly, quarterly, annual, trailing 12-month, or year-to-date snapshot.

description: Total scheduled rental income assuming 100% occupancy at market or contracted rents for the period. Represents the theoretical maximum revenue before vacancy and credit loss deductions. Sourced from Yardi Voyager rent rolls.
reference: NCREIF; Appraisal Institute; Argus Enterprise — Cash Flow Modeling

description: Annual NOI growth rate assumption applied in the DCF model for projecting future cash flows. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0300 = 3.00%). Reflects rent escalation, occupancy improvement, and expense management assumptions.
reference: Argus Enterprise — Cash Flow Modeling; NCREIF

description: Effective gross income divided by the property's net leasable area in square feet. Expressed as currency per square foot (PSF). Benchmarks revenue productivity across the portfolio.
reference: BOMA Standards; NCREIF; CoStar Suite — Property Analytics

description: DCF sensitivity scenario label for this performance record. Base is the primary underwriting case; upside reflects optimistic assumptions; downside reflects conservative assumptions; stress reflects severe adverse conditions.
reference: Argus Enterprise — Investment Analysis; ULI; NCREIF

description: Projected residual value of the asset at the end of the DCF hold period, calculated as terminal year NOI divided by exit CAP rate. Represents the expected sale proceeds at disposition.
reference: Argus Enterprise — Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling; CFA Institute

description: Total investment return for the period combining income return (NOI yield) and capital appreciation return. Expressed as a decimal. NCREIF-standard metric for benchmarking against property indices.
reference: NCREIF Property Index (NPI); CFA Institute; Argus Enterprise

description: Internal Rate of Return calculated on the asset's cash flows before debt financing (unlevered/all-equity basis). Expressed as a decimal. Measures the intrinsic return of the asset independent of capital structure.
reference: NCREIF; CFA Institute; Argus Enterprise — Investment Analysis

description: Timestamp when this asset performance record was last modified. Tracks restatements, corrections, and updates to performance data throughout the record lifecycle.
reference: SOX Financial Controls; GDPR Article 5

description: Deduction from PGI representing income lost due to vacant units and uncollectable rents during the period. Used to derive EGI from PGI.
reference: Appraisal Institute; NCREIF; Argus Enterprise — Cash Flow Modeling

description: Percentage of total leasable area that is unoccupied during the performance period. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0850 = 8.50%). Inverse of occupancy rate; key driver of EGI and NOI.
reference: RESO Data Dictionary; NCREIF; CoStar Suite — Property Analytics

description: Weighted average date on which leases across the asset expire, weighted by rental income or NLA. Expressed as a date. Indicates the point in time when the portfolio faces significant re-leasing risk.
reference: RESO; NCREIF; Argus Enterprise — Lease Management

description: Weighted average remaining lease term across all occupied tenants, weighted by rental income or NLA. Expressed in years. Measures lease duration risk and income security of the asset.
reference: RESO; NCREIF; Argus Enterprise — Lease Management

description: Total Assets Under Management (AUM) for the fund as of the period end date. May differ from GAV when leverage is included or when AUM is defined per the fund's limited partnership agreement. Used for management fee calculations and regulatory reporting.

description: The name of the benchmark index used for performance comparison (e.g., 'NCREIF ODCE', 'MSCI US REIT Index', 'FTSE NAREIT All Equity REITs'). Provides context for interpreting benchmark_return and alpha.

reference: GIPS — CFA Institute; NCREIF; MSCI Real Estate Index

description: The weighted average Capitalization Rate (CAP Rate) applied across the fund's portfolio for the period — NOI divided by GAV. A key real estate valuation metric used in Argus Enterprise models and investor reporting.
reference: Appraisal Institute; IVSC — IVS 105; NAREIT; Argus Enterprise

description: Total Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) incurred by the fund's portfolio during the measurement period, including Tenant Improvement (TI) allowances, building improvements, and major repairs that extend asset life.
reference: NAREIT; FASB ASC 840/842; Yardi Voyager — Fixed Assets

description: The timestamp when this fund performance record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
reference: SOX Section 302; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The discount rate or hurdle rate applied in the fund's DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) valuation models for the period, expressed as a decimal. Used to compute NPV and to assess whether the fund is meeting its return threshold.
reference: Argus Enterprise — Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling; IVSC — IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

description: Cash distribution declared or paid per fund unit or share during the measurement period. Used for investor yield calculations, REIT dividend reporting, and AFFO payout ratio analysis.
reference: NAREIT; SEC Form 10-K; FASB ASC 946; ILPA Reporting Standards

description: Distributions to Paid-In Capital (DPI) ratio — total cumulative distributions paid to investors divided by total paid-in capital. Measures the realized return component. A DPI of 1.0 means investors have received back their full invested capital in cash.
reference: ILPA Reporting Standards; GIPS — CFA Institute

business_glossary_term: Equity Multiple (MOIC — Multiple on Invested Capital)
description: The ratio of total value (realized distributions plus unrealized NAV) to total invested capital, also known as Multiple on Invested Capital (MOIC). A value of 1.75 means investors have received or hold 1.75x their invested capital.
reference: ILPA Reporting Standards; GIPS — CFA Institute

description: Funds From Operations (FFO) for the measurement period — net income plus real estate depreciation and amortization, adjusted for gains/losses on property sales. The NAREIT-defined primary earnings metric for REITs, used in lieu of GAAP net income.
reference: NAREIT FFO White Paper; SEC Form 10-K; FASB ASC 946

description: Gross Asset Value (GAV) of the fund as of the period end date — the sum of appraised market values of all properties and investments held by the fund, before deducting liabilities. Sourced from Argus Enterprise appraisal models.
reference: IVSC — IVS 105; Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 820; ILPA Reporting Standards

business_glossary_term: Gross Internal Rate of Return (Gross IRR)
description: The annualized gross Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for the fund over the measurement period, before management fees and carried interest. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1250 = 12.50%). Core metric for ILPA and SEC reporting.
reference: ILPA Reporting Standards; GIPS — CFA Institute; SEC Form N-2

description: The fund's leverage ratio as of the period end date, typically expressed as total debt divided by GAV (Loan-to-Value / LTV). Monitors compliance with fund-level debt covenants and risk parameters.
reference: ILPA Reporting Standards; SEC Form N-2; FASB ASC 946; Lender Covenant Agreements

description: Money-Weighted Return (MWR) for the measurement period, reflecting the actual investor experience including the timing and magnitude of capital calls and distributions. Equivalent to the period IRR from the investor's perspective.
reference: GIPS — CFA Institute; ILPA Reporting Standards

description: Net Asset Value (NAV) of the fund as of the period end date — GAV minus total liabilities. The primary valuation basis for investor redemptions, unit pricing, and REIT reporting. Sourced from MRI Software and Argus Enterprise.
reference: FASB ASC 946; IVSC; SEC Form N-2; ILPA Reporting Standards

description: The methodology used to determine the NAV for this period. 'independent_appraisal' uses third-party Appraisal Institute-certified appraisers; 'internal_valuation' uses Argus Enterprise DCF models; 'broker_opinion' uses Broker Price Opinion (BPO); 'automated_valuation' uses AVM models; 'hybrid' combines methods.
reference: IVSC — IVS 105; Appraisal Institute USPAP; FASB ASC 820; ILPA Reporting Standards

business_glossary_term: Net Asset Value Per Unit/Share (NAV per Unit)
description: NAV divided by total units or shares outstanding as of the period end date. The per-unit pricing basis for investor subscriptions, redemptions, and REIT share pricing.
reference: FASB ASC 946; SEC Form N-2; ILPA Reporting Standards

business_glossary_term: Net Internal Rate of Return (Net IRR)
description: The annualized net Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for the fund over the measurement period, after deducting management fees, carried interest, and fund expenses. Primary investor-facing performance metric.
reference: ILPA Reporting Standards; GIPS — CFA Institute; SEC Form N-2

description: Net Operating Income (NOI) of the fund's underlying real estate portfolio for the measurement period — total revenue minus operating expenses, before debt service, depreciation, and income taxes. Core metric for real estate valuation and CAP rate analysis.
reference: NAREIT; Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 946; Argus Enterprise

description: Net Present Value (NPV) of the fund's projected cash flows discounted at the fund's hurdle rate or discount rate as of the period end date. Sourced from Argus Enterprise DCF models.

description: The maximum annual CPI escalation rate permitted under the lease terms, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 = 5.00% cap). Protects the tenant from excessive CPI-driven rent increases. Null for uncapped CPI or non-CPI escalation types.
reference: FASB ASC 842; Yardi Voyager Lease Administration

business_glossary_term: Consumer Price Index (CPI) Escalation Floor Rate
description: The minimum annual CPI escalation rate guaranteed under the lease terms, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0200 = 2.00% floor). Protects the landlord from zero or negative CPI adjustments. Null for non-CPI escalation types.
reference: FASB ASC 842; Yardi Voyager Lease Administration

description: The name of the CPI index used for rent escalation when escalation_type is 'cpi' (e.g., 'US CPI-U All Items', 'UK RPI'). Null for non-CPI escalation types.

description: The timestamp when this rent schedule record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance controls.
reference: SOX; FASB ASC 842; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

description: The discount rate used to calculate the present value of lease payments for this rent step under ASC 842 / IFRS 16. Typically the implicit rate in the lease or the lessee's incremental borrowing rate (IBR). Expressed as a decimal annual rate (e.g., 0.0450 = 4.50%).

description: The last date on which this rent step period is in effect. The next step's effective_start_date should immediately follow. Null for open-ended final steps.

description: The mechanism by which rent increases from one step to the next. 'fixed_step' = predetermined dollar or percentage increase; 'cpi' = Consumer Price Index-linked; 'percentage_of_sales' = percentage rent tied to tenant gross sales; 'market_review' = reset to fair market value; 'none' = flat rent with no escalation.

description: The percentage rate applied to the overdue rent balance to calculate the late payment fee after the grace period expires. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 = 5.00%). Null if a flat late fee amount applies instead.

description: Number of dependents enrolled under the employee's benefit plan election. Used for coverage tier validation, carrier eligibility feeds, and ACA 1095-C Part III reporting.
reference: ACA Section 1001; IRS Form 1095-C; ADP Workforce Now

description: Indicates whether the employee has elected dependent coverage under this benefit plan. True when one or more dependents are enrolled. Drives ACA 1095-C Part III dependent reporting requirements.
reference: ACA Section 1001; IRS Form 1095-C; ADP Workforce Now

description: Percentage of the employee's base salary replaced by the disability benefit plan (short-term or long-term disability). Applicable when plan_type = 'disability'. Used in total compensation reporting and workforce planning.

description: Date on which the employee's coverage under this benefit plan ends. Null for currently active enrollments. Triggers COBRA notification requirements upon termination of coverage.

reference: ACA Section 4980H; ERISA; IRS Publication 15-B; ADP Workforce Now

description: Textual description of the eligibility rules for this benefit plan, including minimum hours worked, employment classification (full-time, part-time), waiting period, and applicable employee groups (e.g., property managers, brokers, corporate staff).
reference: ERISA; ACA Section 4980H; IRS Publication 15-B; ADP Workforce Now

business_glossary_term: Employee Health Savings Account (HSA) Contribution Amount
description: Annual employee contribution amount elected for a Health Savings Account (HSA). Applicable only when plan_type = 'HSA'. Subject to IRS annual contribution limits. Used for payroll deduction and W-2 Box 12 reporting.
reference: IRS Section 223; IRS Publication 969; ADP Workforce Now

description: Per-pay-period premium amount deducted from the employee's paycheck for this benefit plan. Used for payroll deduction configuration and benefits cost allocation reporting.
reference: IRS Section 125; ADP Workforce Now Payroll; FASB ASC 715

business_glossary_term: Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) Contribution Amount
description: Annual employer seed contribution to the employee's Health Savings Account (HSA). Applicable only when plan_type = 'HSA'. Reported on W-2 Box 12 Code W.
reference: IRS Section 223; IRS Publication 969; ADP Workforce Now

description: Textual description of the employer's 401(k) matching contribution formula (e.g., '100% match on first 3% of compensation, 50% match on next 2%'). Applicable when plan_type = '401k'. Used in employee communications and total compensation reporting.
reference: IRS Section 401(k); ERISA; ADP Workforce Now

description: Maximum percentage of eligible compensation the employer will match under the 401(k) plan. Used for benefits cost modeling, OPEX budgeting, and total compensation analytics.
reference: IRS Section 401(k); ERISA; ADP Workforce Now

description: Per-pay-period premium amount contributed by the employer for this benefit plan. Used for benefits cost allocation to property management, development, and corporate cost centers (OPEX tracking).
reference: FASB ASC 715; IRS Publication 15-B; ADP Workforce Now; SAP S/4HANA Cost Allocation

description: The triggering event that initiated this benefit enrollment or change. Determines the enrollment window and permissible elections under IRS and ERISA rules.
reference: ERISA Section 701; IRS Section 125; ACA; ADP Workforce Now

description: Current status of the employee's enrollment in this benefit plan. Enrolled indicates active coverage; waived indicates the employee declined coverage; COBRA_elected indicates post-termination continuation coverage.
reference: ERISA; COBRA; ACA 1095-C; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Timestamp when the benefit enrollment record was first created in ADP Workforce Now. Serves as the audit trail anchor for the enrollment lifecycle and supports SOX financial controls over payroll deductions.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; ADP Workforce Now; ERISA

description: Annual employee contribution amount elected for a Flexible Spending Account (FSA). Applicable when plan_type = 'FSA'. Subject to IRS annual contribution limits and use-it-or-lose-it rules.
reference: IRS Section 125; IRS Publication 969; ADP Workforce Now

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the benefit enrollment record in ADP Workforce Now. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver layer ingestion pipeline and audit trail maintenance.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; ADP Workforce Now; ERISA

description: Face value of life insurance coverage elected by the employee. Applicable when plan_type = 'life'. Amounts exceeding $50,000 of employer-paid coverage are subject to imputed income under IRS Section 79.
reference: IRS Section 79; IRS Publication 15-B; ADP Workforce Now

description: Maximum annual out-of-pocket cost the employee is responsible for under the plan, after which the plan covers 100% of covered expenses. ACA-mandated limit for qualified health plans.
reference: ACA Section 1302; IRS Publication 15-B; ADP Workforce Now

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code assigned to the benefit plan by the carrier or the enterprise HR system (ADP Workforce Now). Used as the business identifier for plan lookup and cross-system reconciliation.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; IRS Publication 15-B

description: Human-readable name of the benefit plan as presented to employees (e.g., 'Aetna PPO Gold', 'Delta Dental Premier', 'Fidelity 401(k) Plan'). Used in employee-facing communications and ACA reporting.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; ACA 1095-C Reporting

description: Current lifecycle state of the benefit plan offering. Active plans are available for enrollment; terminated plans are closed to new elections; suspended plans are temporarily unavailable.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; ERISA

reference: IRS Publication 15-B; ACA Section 4980H; ERISA; ADP Workforce Now

description: Calendar or fiscal year for which this benefit plan is offered (e.g., 2024). Used to segment plan configurations, premium rates, and enrollment windows by year for ACA 1095-C reporting and cost allocation.
reference: IRS Publication 15-B; ACA Section 6055/6056; ADP Workforce Now

description: Last day of the benefit plan year. Defines when current coverage terms, premium rates, and contribution limits expire. Used for COBRA administration and ACA reporting period boundaries.
reference: ERISA; IRS Publication 15-B; ACA Section 4980H; COBRA

description: First day of the benefit plan year. Defines the effective start of coverage terms, premium rates, deductibles, and contribution limits for the plan year.
reference: ERISA; IRS Publication 15-B; ACA Section 4980H

description: Frequency at which premium contributions are deducted from payroll or billed to the employer. Must align with the payroll cycle configured in ADP Workforce Now.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Payroll; IRS Publication 15

description: Employee's elected contribution rate as a percentage of eligible compensation for the 401(k) or retirement plan. Applicable when plan_type = '401k'. Used for payroll deduction calculation and IRS annual limit compliance.
reference: IRS Section 401(k); ERISA; ADP Workforce Now

description: Total per-pay-period premium for this benefit plan (employee + employer contributions combined). Used for carrier billing reconciliation and total benefits cost reporting.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; ERISA; FASB ASC 715

description: Number of months of service required before employer contributions begin to vest under a cliff or graded vesting schedule. Applicable when vesting_schedule_type is 'cliff' or 'graded'.
reference: ERISA Section 203; IRS Section 411; ADP Workforce Now

description: Total months of service required for the employee to become 100% vested in employer contributions. Used for workforce retention analytics and ERISA compliance reporting.
reference: ERISA Section 203; IRS Section 411; ADP Workforce Now

description: Type of vesting schedule applied to employer contributions in the retirement plan. Immediate vesting grants full ownership at once; cliff vesting grants full ownership after a defined period; graded vesting grants incremental ownership over time.
reference: ERISA Section 203; IRS Section 411; ADP Workforce Now

description: Number of days from the employee's hire date or qualifying event before coverage under this benefit plan becomes effective. ACA limits waiting periods to 90 days for employer-sponsored health plans.
reference: ACA Section 2708; IRS Notice 2012-59; ADP Workforce Now

description: Indicates whether the employee has affirmatively waived coverage under this benefit plan. True when the employee declined enrollment. Required for ACA 1095-C Line 16 reporting to document offer and waiver.
reference: ACA Section 6056; IRS Form 1095-C; ADP Workforce Now

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each benefit enrollment record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the benefit_enrollment data product.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Reference to the benefit plan in which the employee is enrolling or waiving. Links to the benefit plan master record (e.g., medical, dental, vision, 401k, FSA, HSA, life insurance).
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Reference to the finance cost center to which the employer's benefit contribution cost for this enrollment is allocated. Enables benefits OPEX allocation across real estate business units such as property management, development, brokerage, and corporate functions. Links to the finance cost center master.
reference: FASB ASC 715; SAP S/4HANA Cost Center Accounting; SOX Financial Controls

description: Reference to the employee who elected or waived this benefit plan. Links to the workforce employee master record sourced from ADP Workforce Now.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

business_glossary_term: ACA Offer of Coverage Type Code
description: The IRS-defined code indicating the type of health coverage offered to the employee for ACA Form 1095-C Line 14 reporting (e.g., 1A through 1I). Identifies whether minimum essential coverage was offered to the employee only, employee and dependents, or not offered. Required for ACA employer shared responsibility compliance for real estate employers with 50+ full-time equivalent employees.
reference: IRS Form 1095-C Instructions; IRC § 4980H; ACA Employer Shared Responsibility

description: The IRS-defined code for ACA Form 1095-C Line 16 indicating the applicable safe harbor or relief provision (e.g., 2A through 2I). Used to indicate months the employee was not employed, was in a waiting period, or the employer qualifies for an affordability safe harbor. Required for ACA employer shared responsibility reporting.
reference: IRS Form 1095-C Instructions; IRC § 4980H; IRS Notice 2015-87

description: The annualized employee premium cost for this benefit enrollment, calculated as the per-period employee contribution multiplied by the number of pay periods in the plan year. Used for ACA affordability testing (employee cost must not exceed a percentage of household income) and total compensation reporting.
reference: IRS ACA Affordability Rules (IRC § 36B); ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The annualized employer contribution toward this benefit enrollment for the plan year. Used for OPEX budgeting, benefits cost allocation across real estate business units, and FASB ASC 715 disclosure.
reference: FASB ASC 715; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; SOX

description: The date and time when the benefit enrollment was approved by HR or the benefits administrator. Null if the enrollment is pending approval or was auto-approved. Supports audit trail requirements and enrollment processing SLA tracking.
reference: ERISA; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The unique member identification number assigned by the insurance carrier or benefit plan provider to the enrolled employee. Used for claims processing, eligibility verification, and carrier EDI 834 enrollment file reconciliation. Distinct from the internal ADP employee ID.
reference: HIPAA EDI 834 Benefit Enrollment Transaction; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The deadline by which the qualified beneficiary must elect COBRA continuation coverage following a qualifying event. Typically 60 days from the later of the qualifying event date or the date the COBRA election notice was provided. Null if cobra_eligible is False or no qualifying event has occurred.
reference: COBRA (29 U.S.C. § 1165); DOL COBRA Regulations

description: Indicates whether this enrollment is eligible for COBRA continuation coverage upon a qualifying event (e.g., employment termination, reduction in hours). True for group health plans subject to COBRA; False for plans exempt from COBRA (e.g., dental-only, vision-only under certain thresholds, or employers with fewer than 20 employees).
reference: COBRA (29 U.S.C. § 1161); DOL COBRA Regulations; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The pay period frequency at which employee and employer contributions are applied for this enrollment. Determines how per-period amounts are annualized for ACA affordability testing and benefits cost reporting.
reference: IRS ACA Affordability Safe Harbors; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The coverage tier elected by the employee, defining who is covered under the benefit plan. Employee Only covers the employee alone; Employee + Spouse adds a spouse or domestic partner; Employee + Children adds dependent children; Employee + Family covers all eligible dependents. Drives premium contribution calculations and ACA affordability testing.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; IRS ACA Affordability Rules; ERISA

description: The date and time when this benefit enrollment record was first created in the system. Serves as the record audit creation timestamp for data lineage, Silver Layer ingestion tracking, and SOX audit trail requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; GDPR Article 5

description: The number of dependents (spouse, domestic partner, children) covered under this enrollment. Used to validate coverage tier elections, calculate per-dependent costs, and support ACA dependent coverage reporting for children up to age 26.
reference: ACA Section 2714 (Dependent Coverage to Age 26); ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The date on which the benefit coverage becomes active for the employee under this enrollment. Determines when premium deductions begin and when claims can be submitted. Critical for ACA minimum essential coverage (MEC) determination and 1095-C line 14/15/16 reporting.
reference: IRS ACA Reporting; ERISA; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The date and time when the employee submitted their benefit election or waiver. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for this enrollment transaction. Used for audit trails, late enrollment identification, and compliance with enrollment window deadlines.
reference: ERISA; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; HIPAA Special Enrollment Rules

description: The date on which the employee first became eligible to enroll in this benefit plan, typically based on hire date plus any applicable waiting period (e.g., 30, 60, or 90 days). Used to validate enrollment timeliness and ACA waiting period compliance (maximum 90-day waiting period rule).
reference: ACA 90-Day Waiting Period Rule (IRC § 9815); ERISA; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The per-pay-period pre-tax or post-tax dollar amount deducted from the employee's paycheck for this benefit plan enrollment. Used for payroll deduction processing, benefits cost allocation across real estate cost centers (property management, development, corporate), and W-2 Box 12 reporting.
reference: IRS Section 125; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; FASB ASC 715

description: The per-pay-period dollar amount contributed by the employer toward this benefit plan enrollment. Used for benefits cost allocation to property management, development, and corporate OPEX budgets, and for FASB ASC 715 post-employment benefit accounting.
reference: FASB ASC 715; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; SOX Financial Controls

description: The employment classification of the employee at the time of enrollment. Determines benefit eligibility rules; full-time employees (30+ hours per week) are subject to ACA employer mandate; part-time employees may have limited benefit eligibility. Relevant for real estate roles including property managers, leasing agents, brokers, and construction staff.
reference: IRS ACA Full-Time Employee Definition (IRC § 4980H); ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: The triggering event that initiated this benefit enrollment or change. New hire enrollments occur within the initial eligibility window; open enrollment occurs during the annual election period; qualifying life events (QLE) include marriage, birth, divorce, or loss of other coverage; rehire triggers a new enrollment window; COBRA enrollments apply to terminated employees electing continuation coverage.
reference: IRS Section 125; ERISA; HIPAA Special Enrollment; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Externally-known unique enrollment reference number assigned by ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration. Used for cross-system reconciliation, ACA 1095-C reporting, and COBRA administration correspondence.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; IRS ACA Reporting

description: The channel or method through which the benefit enrollment was submitted. Self-service indicates the employee enrolled via the ADP employee self-service portal; hr_admin indicates HR staff entered the election on behalf of the employee; paper_form indicates a physical enrollment form was submitted; api_integration indicates enrollment was received via system integration; auto_enrolled indicates the employee was automatically enrolled per plan rules.
reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Current lifecycle state of the benefit enrollment record. description: The per-period employer contribution to the employee's Health Savings Account (HSA), applicable when the employee is enrolled in a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP). reference: IRS HSA Contribution Limits (IRC § 223); IRS Form W-2 Box 12 Code W; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

reference: ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration; ERISA

description: The date on which the qualifying life event (QLE) occurred that triggered a mid-year enrollment change outside of open enrollment. reference: HIPAA Special Enrollment (29 CFR § 2590.701-6); IRS Section 125; ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

Null for new hire and open enrollment event types.
reference: HIPAA Special Enrollment (29 CFR § 2590.701-6); IRS Section 125; ERISA

reference: ACA 90-Day Waiting Period Rule (IRC § 9815); ADP Workforce Now Benefits Administration

description: Indicates whether the employee affirmatively declined (waived) coverage under this benefit plan for the plan year. True means the employee opted out; False means the employee enrolled.
